findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, and no ACL is set, meaning stored data (including the vendor-roster.xlsx object) is not encrypted at rest and the bucket relies on default (potentially public/legacy) ACL behavior.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving ledger export data unencrypted at rest despite being a sensitive financial dataset.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving operational runbook content (which may include sensitive operational procedures/credentials references) unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL; this is likely a typo intended to be 'log-delivery-write', but as configured it may fail or default to an unintended access setting, risking unexpected access control behavior on a sensitive audit trail bucket.
The object is uploaded to a bucket (reports_archive) that has no default encryption configured, and the object itself specifies no server_side_encryption, so this file is stored in cleartext at rest.

findings.issue_category: force destroy enabled on data bucket
findings.description: force_destroy = true combined with no encryption or explicit access controls increases risk of irrecoverable data exposure/loss pathways when the bucket is deleted, but more critically the bucket lacks any explicit private ACL or public access block, leaving default visibility ambiguous.
